verdict_text: YES. The plan deletes exactly the 28 tensors of blocks 2, 6, 10, 14 (guarded by a count assert), then renames the survivors in ascending destination order (3→2, 4→3, 5→4, 7→5, 8→6, 9→7, 11→8, 12→9, 13→10, 15→11), so every destination index is already vacated by a prior delete or move and no block overwrites a surviving one; the mapping matches clause 2 exactly, and only the block index changes since the rest of the name is carried through the capture group. The two non-block tensors are never touched, and the three required checks are present as asserts (no blocks 12–15 remain, exactly 12 q_proj tensors, 86 tensors total), placed after the renumbering so a failure aborts before the output is written. The literal `model\.layers\.` prefix in each pattern prevents the single-digit patterns from matching two-digit indices such as `model.layers.13.`. Output goes to the required single file `out/T1/model.safetensors`.
